title: GarmentWeaver: Schema-Aware Structured Synthesis for Multimodal Sewing Patterns
abstract: Multimodal Sewing pattern generation aims to infer executable sewing patterns from design cues such as sketches and textual descriptions. As an interpretable and simulation-compatible representation, sewing patterns are particularly valuable for digital garment creation. However, existing methods often model garment specifications as flat long sequences, which entangles garment structure with detailed parameters and leads to redundant components, inaccurate local details, and poor simulation compatibility. In this paper, we present GarmentWeaver, a schema-aware framework for multimodal Sewing pattern generation. GarmentWeaver constructs compact hierarchical targets by activating garment-relevant structural branches and predicts executable Sewing patterns in a structured manner. Specifically, we introduce a schema-aware target construction strategy, build the generator on top of a pretrained vision-language model for multimodal garment understanding, and impose feasibility-aware regularization to encourage structurally valid and simulation-compatible outputs. Extensive experiments show that GarmentWeaver produces more accurate and more executable sewing patterns than strong baselines, while also yielding better simulation results. These findings demonstrate the effectiveness of schema-aware structured generation for reliable multimodal Sewing pattern prediction.

title: Coarse composition suffices: tabular in-context learning for multi-activity antimicrobial peptide profiling
abstract: Antimicrobial peptides (AMPs) often act against multiple pathogen classes, making multi-label activity prediction a more realistic screening target than binary antimicrobial classification. The ESCAPE benchmark formalizes this setting, but leading approaches typically rely on multimodal, structure-conditioned deep models that are costly to train and tune. We show that a simple, sequence-only pipeline can match and surpass these methods by combining 330 interpretable sequence descriptors with TabPFN, a tabular foundation model that performs in-context prediction in a single forward pass without gradient-based training or hyperparameter search. On ESCAPE (82,359 peptides; five labels), a label-powerset TabPFN model achieves mAP-5 = 77.8%, improving on the previously best reported 72.1%. A probabilistic classifier chain is the first method to match or exceed the best published average precision on each of the five labels simultaneously. The gains persist under the prior state-of-the-art single-fold training protocol, indicating they are not a training-set-size artefact, and are largest for remote homologues (+11.2 points below 30% sequence identity). Ablations further show that predicted structure is unnecessary at inference and that performance is not driven by any single descriptor family: ten global physicochemical scalars recover 91% of full-feature performance. Finally, explicitly modelling label dependence yields targeted benefits for scarce activities and supports ranking which activity to assay next from partial positive evidence.

title: Corpus of the Gail Valley dialect Zila 1.0
abstract: The Zila Speech Corpus is a spoken language resource documenting the Slovenian Gail Valley dialect, an endangered Slovenian minority dialect spoken in Austria. The corpus contains 206 recordings in WAV format, with a total duration of approximately 100 hours and 7 minutes, produced by 74 anonymized speakers. It was created within the LINGUA project to support the development of automatic speech recognition for the Gail Valley dialect, as well as linguistic research, education, corpus search, and long-term dialect documentation and preservation. The corpus includes different types of speech material: private speech, public informal speech, public formal speech, and read speech. The largest part of the corpus consists of private recordings, while the remaining material documents public, institutional, and read speech contexts. The recordings cover topics such as autobiographical narratives, Gail Valley identity, folk tales, local customs and rituals, rural work and farming, family and village networks, local history, memories, and community life. The recordings in WAV format are accompanied by manually prepared, time-aligned transcriptions in Transcriber .trs format. The transcription follows an extended orthographic approach: dialectal morphological and syntactic features, hesitations, fillers, and self-corrections are preserved, while the transcription is not intended as a full phonetic transcription. Personal data in the transcripts are anonymized using the marker [anonim], and the corresponding sections in the audio are masked with a beep before publication. Beside the .trs format, the transcriptions in EXMARaLDA format (.exb, .exs) were also generated. Speaker metadata include anonymized speaker ID, gender, age, first language, bilingualism, dialect information, dialect retention, education, residence information, spontaneity of speech, and notes. Recording metadata include recording and transcription identifiers, language, title, date, source, recording location, genre, speech type, channel, number of speakers, recording device, recording setting, original format, audio quality, length, and notes.

title: Temporal Attention-Based Transformer-LSTM Hybrid Deep Learning Model for Solar Power Generation Forecasting
abstract: In response to climate change and the global transition toward carbon neutrality, accurate solar power generation forecasting has become increasingly important, as forecast accuracy directly affects the economic value of electricity trading and carbon emission markets. This study proposes a temporal attention-based Transformer-LSTM hybrid model that integrates the Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) network, which is effective in capturing short-term temporal dependencies, with the Transformer, which provides superior long-range dependency modeling and parallelizable computation. In the preprocessing stage, missing values in ten meteorological variables were imputed via hybrid imputation approach including zero-masking and linear interpolation, and the data were subsequently normalized using min-max scaling. To further improve forecasting accuracy, four time features (sine and cosine transformations of hour and day) were incorporated, and a temporal attention mechanism was employed to enable the model to selectively attend to the past time steps most relevant to the current prediction. In experiments on a 168-hour (one-week) forecasting horizon, the proposed model achieved a coefficient of determination (R²) of 0.8924 (89.24%), outperforming the standalone LSTM (0.8029, 80.29%) and Transformer (0.8123, 81.23%). Under identical experimental conditions, the proposed model also surpassed representative time-series forecasting models, including XGBoost, the Temporal Fusion Transformer (TFT), and PatchTST. These results indicate that the incorporation of the four time features and the selective attention to influential past time steps enable the proposed model to achieve higher solar power forecasting accuracy than existing approaches.

title: Deep Neuro-Fuzzy Architectures: Interpretable Fuzzy Models and Routed Kolmogorov–Arnold Fuzzy Networks (Интерпретируемые глубокие нейро-нечёткие модели и маршрутизируемые нечёткие сети Колмогорова–Арнольда)
abstract: Deep Neuro-Fuzzy Architectures v1.1.0 Публичная версия исследовательского программного комплекса для разработки, сравнения и воспроизводимой оценки интерпретируемых глубоких нейро-нечётких моделей. Текущая работа сфокусирована на Routed Kolmogorov–Arnold Fuzzy Networks (Routed KAFN) и сравнении различных архитектур глубоких нечётких систем по качеству прогнозирования, сложности и структурной устойчивости. Реализованные архитектуры Shallow Fuzzy; Stacked Fuzzy; Hierarchical Fuzzy; Deep Fuzzy Feature Learning (DFFL); Routed KAFN. Routed KAFN Routed KAFN использует маршрутизируемые аддитивные одномерные нечёткие предикаты вместо полного комбинаторного многомерного пространства правил ANFIS-подобных моделей. Маршруты признаков определяются до нейронного обучения на основе важности признаков Extra Trees. Архитектура поддерживает фиксированные projection-pursuit каналы для ограниченного моделирования взаимодействий между признаками. Основная исследуемая характеристика Routed KAFN — компромисс между: качеством классификации; сложностью нечёткой структуры; интерпретируемостью; воспроизводимостью активной структуры между повторными запусками. Основные результаты На covtype_binary_20000 Routed KAFN с фиксированными проекциями показал: F1: 0.8174 ± 0.0101; ROC-AUC: 0.8857 ± 0.0035; PR-AUC: 0.8605 ± 0.0022; Jaccard стабильности активных предикатов: 0.9167. Для сравнения, Stacked Fuzzy показал несколько более высокий F1 (0.8222 ± 0.0074), но существенно меньшую структурную стабильность (Jaccard = 0.0978). Таким образом, Routed KAFN не рассматривается как универсально превосходящая по точности архитектура. Основной результат заключается в достижении конкурентного качества при значительно более воспроизводимой активной нечёткой структуре. Дополнительная крупномасштабная проверка выполнена на Covtype, SUSY-200k и KDDCup99-10%. Воспроизводимость Репозиторий содержит: библиотечную реализацию нейро-нечётких моделей; экспериментальные и benchmark-сценарии; автоматизированные тесты; конфигурации экспериментов; компактные итоговые артефакты; рисунки и материалы для научных публикаций; инструкции по подготовке данных и воспроизведению результатов. Исходные наборы данных и необработанные результаты запусков в репозиторий не включаются. Лицензия Программное обеспечение распространяется по лицензии MIT.

title: Quantum Morphic Geometry for Geometric Computation
abstract: Quantum morphic geometry offers a novel approach to geometric computation, leveraging the principles of quantum mechanics and geometry to perform complex transformations. This paper introduces a framework based on quantum morphic fields, demonstrating its potential for efficient computation through quantum algorithms. We explore the core mechanism of utilizing quantum morphic fields to simulate geometric transformations and integrate quantum algorithms for enhanced computational efficiency. The research focuses on providing a robust and scalable method for geometric manipulation, potentially revolutionizing existing computational techniques.

title: Dynamic Probability Field Driven Optimization, Based on Gaussian Processes
abstract: This paper introduces a novel dynamic probability field driven optimization algorithm, designed to address complex optimization problems with enhanced efficiency. Traditional optimization methods often struggle with dynamic and intricate optimization scenarios. This work leverages the power of Gaussian processes to transform the dynamic probability field into a dynamically evolving optimization process, accelerating the optimization process and improving overall efficiency. We present a robust and effective algorithm that exhibits superior performance compared to existing approaches across a range of benchmark problems. The core mechanism centers around the utilization of Gaussian processes for efficient trajectory mapping and parameter estimation, leading to a streamlined optimization pathway. The paper details the algorithm's design, implementation, and comprehensive evaluation on several challenging optimization tasks.

title: Quantum Walk-Based Search Algorithms for Massive Datasets
abstract: This paper investigates the application of quantum walk-based search algorithms to address the scalability challenges inherent in classical search algorithms when dealing with massive datasets. The core premise is that quantum superposition and interference, inherent properties of quantum systems, offer a potential pathway to significantly enhance the efficiency of search operations. We propose and analyze quantum walk algorithms designed to explore search spaces more effectively than their classical counterparts. The focus is on theoretical development and algorithmic design, without experimental validation. We explore key concepts such as walker position, probability amplitudes, and interference effects within the framework of quantum walks. The algorithms are designed to be adaptable to both quantum hardware and quantum simulators. This work aims to demonstrate the theoretical feasibility and potential advantages of utilizing quantum walk algorithms for large-scale data search, contributing to the growing field of quantum search algorithms.

title: 基于遗传算法的非线性拓扑系统优化
abstract: This paper investigates the application of genetic algorithms (GAs) to optimize non-linear topological systems. Non-linear topological systems often present significant challenges in design and analysis, requiring sophisticated optimization techniques. Traditional optimization methods may struggle with the complex, non-linear nature of these systems. This work proposes a novel approach utilizing GAs to explore the vast solution space of these systems, leading to improved performance metrics. The core of the research involves the implementation of a GA framework that iteratively evolves a population of potential solutions, guided by a fitness function that evaluates the system's behavior. We demonstrate the effectiveness of this approach through simulations and preliminary results, showcasing the potential for GAs to effectively optimize these complex topological systems.

The core mechanism centers around the QNN's adaptive learning capabilities, allowing for the identification of intricate structure patterns and subsequent predictive and control capabilities. Traditional methods often rely on manual design, limiting the scope of analysis. This work explores the potential of QNNs to automate and enhance topological structure mapping, offering a significant advancement in understanding and manipulating complex systems. The paper details the QNN architecture, its training process, and preliminary results demonstrating its effectiveness in identifying and predicting topological transformations.

title: Quantum Error Correction Coding and Information Gain Optimization
abstract: This paper investigates a novel approach to quantum information transmission by integrating quantum error correction coding with dynamic information gain optimization. The core claim is that by adapting the parameters of quantum error correction codes based on the observed state of quantum information during transmission, it is possible to achieve optimal information gain. The proposed mechanism leverages the inherent redundancy of quantum error correction to not only mitigate errors but also to dynamically adjust the coding scheme, maximizing the overall reliability and efficiency of the transmission process. This represents a new strategy for quantum information transfer, moving beyond static error correction protocols and toward a more adaptive and optimized system. The key mathematical framework presented here focuses on quantifying information gain, defining error correction parameters, and outlining the iterative process of adjustment based on transmission feedback. The potential impact of this approach is significant for applications requiring high-fidelity quantum communication, particularly in challenging environments with high noise levels.

title: Non-commutative Group Structures and Adaptive Self-Organizing Algorithms
abstract: This paper introduces a novel dynamic self-organizing algorithm based on non-commutative group structures. Traditional optimization methods rely on manual design, while this approach leverages the inherent dynamic properties of non-commutative groups to autonomously explore system structures and dynamically adjust parameters for enhanced optimization results. The algorithm iteratively calculates and adapts to the structure of the non-commutative group, leading to improved performance compared to conventional methods. We detail the core mechanism, emphasizing the use of group-specific properties to guide parameter adjustments. This research contributes to a new paradigm in optimization, offering a robust and automated approach to discovering optimal solutions within complex systems.

title: Dynamic Adaptive Dimensionality Space Analysis Method
abstract: This paper introduces a dynamic adaptive dimensionality space analysis method designed to enhance the expressiveness and computational efficiency of mathematical models. Traditional methods often rely on manual design, limiting the potential for automated insight. This novel approach leverages a dynamic adjustment process, powered by machine learning, to automatically identify and adjust key dimensions within the mathematical structure. The core mechanism centers around a continuous refinement of the dimensionality space, guided by a learned model. We present a comprehensive investigation of the method's effectiveness through extensive analysis and experimental validation. The paper details the methodology, its implementation, and the resulting improvements in model representation and computational performance.

abstract: This paper introduces a novel optimization algorithm based on quantum entanglement principles to address complex system optimization problems. The algorithm leverages quantum entanglement to enhance the efficiency of solving intricate optimization tasks, particularly those involving multiple variables and constraints. We demonstrate its effectiveness through a series of rigorous simulations and analyses, highlighting its potential to significantly outperform traditional optimization methods in various real-world scenarios. The core mechanism centers around introducing quantum entanglement during the optimization process, enabling the algorithm to explore a wider solution space and effectively navigate complex landscapes. This work represents a significant advancement in optimization techniques, holding promise for applications across diverse fields.

title: Title: Adaptive Topology for Reinforcement Learning Agents
abstract: The design of environments in reinforcement learning is often constrained by the need for efficient exploration and faster learning. Traditional approaches often rely on pre-defined topologies, which can limit agent exploration and hinder learning. This paper introduces an adaptive topology system designed to dynamically adjust the environment's topology during reinforcement learning, aiming to improve agent exploration and learning speed. We propose a neural network-based approach that learns the optimal topology for each agent, adapting the network structure based on the agent's experience. The core mechanism leverages the power of neural networks to create a flexible and responsive environment, addressing a long-standing challenge in reinforcement learning. This work provides a novel method for enhancing the robustness and efficiency of reinforcement learning agents.

title: Title: Dynamically Constructed Quantum States – Adaptive Resonance
abstract: This paper presents a novel quantum algorithm, "Dynamic State Adjustment," designed to generate complex quantum states that dynamically adapt to environmental fluctuations. The core concept revolves around a self-regulating system that continuously analyzes the state of a quantum system and adjusts it to maintain stability, thereby producing complex and resilient quantum states. The algorithm's primary objective is to overcome the limitations of static quantum state representations, which often struggle to maintain stability in dynamic environments. We detail the implementation of this system and demonstrate its effectiveness through theoretical analysis and preliminary simulations. The focus is on creating stable and complex quantum states that exhibit enhanced resilience.

title: Belligerent Horseshoe Bat: A Novel Metaheuristic Algorithm Inspired by the Defensive Behavior of *Rhinolophus ferrumequinum*
abstract: This paper presents Belligerent Horseshoe Bat (BHSB), a new metaheuristic optimization algorithm inspired by the defensive behavior of *Rhinolophus ferrumequinum*, a species of horseshoe bat known for its aggressive territorial defense. BHSB mimics the bat's rapid, evasive maneuvers and strategic positioning to navigate complex and dynamic environments. The algorithm incorporates three core mechanisms: (1) a 'Charge' operator, simulating the bat's direct attack on potential threats, (2) an 'Evasion' operator, modeling the bat's quick changes in direction and position, and (3) a 'Territorial Marking' operator, representing the bat's use of scent marking to establish and defend its territory. These mechanisms are combined within a population-based search framework, utilizing a modified version of the Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO) algorithm. The performance of BHSB is evaluated across a diverse set of benchmark optimization problems, demonstrating its effectiveness in finding optimal or near-optimal solutions. The results indicate that BHSB outperforms several established metaheuristic algorithms in terms of convergence speed and solution quality. Finally, the paper explores the algorithm's parameters and their impact on performance, providing insights into its design and potential for further development.

title: Quantum Sensing with Multi-Variable Measurement
abstract: This paper explores the development and potential of quantum sensors utilizing multi-variable measurement. The core concept revolves around leveraging the quantum coherence inherent in quantum sensors to simultaneously measure multiple physical quantities. This is achieved through the design of entangled sensor networks, where the state of one sensor provides information about the states of all interconnected sensors. This approach represents a significant advancement in the field of quantum sensing, offering the possibility of enhanced sensitivity and reduced measurement complexity for applications requiring the simultaneous determination of multiple parameters. The theoretical framework presented here outlines the fundamental principles and explores potential architectures, highlighting the advantages and challenges associated with this technology. We focus on the mathematical underpinnings of entangled sensor systems and the extraction of information from correlated quantum states. ---

title: Baoule's Mouse: A Metaheuristic Algorithm Inspired by the Navigational Behavior of Mice
abstract: This paper introduces Baoule's Mouse, a novel metaheuristic optimization algorithm inspired by the navigational behavior of mice. Mice are renowned for their ability to efficiently find routes to food sources, utilizing a combination of exploration and exploitation strategies. Baoule's Mouse mimics these behaviors by employing a "mouse" agent that explores the search space and exploits promising regions. The algorithm utilizes a path representation, a "trail" following, and a "pheromone" mechanism to guide the agent's movement. The core of the algorithm lies in a stochastic path selection process influenced by a "hunger" factor and a "memory" component, representing the mouse's need to find food and its recollection of past successful routes. We present the algorithm's theoretical framework, detailing the key parameters and their impact on performance. Simulation results demonstrate the effectiveness of Baoule's Mouse on a range of benchmark optimization problems, showcasing its competitive performance compared to established metaheuristic algorithms. The algorithm's simplicity and adaptability make it a promising approach for various optimization challenges.

title: Balabac Chevrotain: A Novel Metaheuristic Algorithm Inspired by the Foraging Behavior of the Balabac Chevrotain
abstract: This paper presents a novel metaheuristic optimization algorithm, termed the Balabac Chevrotain Algorithm (BCA), inspired by the foraging behavior of the Balabac Chevrotain (Tragulus luc browni), a small chevrotain species found in the Philippines. The algorithm leverages the animal's efficient exploration and exploitation strategies for navigating complex environments and locating food sources. BCA incorporates key aspects of the chevrotain's behavior, including its reliance on scent trails, rapid directional changes, and a tendency to revisit promising areas. Specifically, the algorithm utilizes a modified Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO) framework, incorporating a novel 'Scent Trail' mechanism to guide particle movement, a 'Rapid Shift' operator for diversification, and an 'Area Revisit' strategy based on probabilistic revisit rates. The performance of BCA is evaluated across a range of benchmark optimization problems, demonstrating its effectiveness in finding near-optimal solutions with competitive efficiency compared to established metaheuristic methods. The algorithm's design aims to provide a robust and adaptable solution for diverse optimization challenges. The core objective is to mimic the chevrotain's adaptive behavior to create an effective optimization tool.

abstract: This paper introduces a novel machine learning model based on self-organizing networks, designed to predict the behavior of complex systems. Traditional machine learning models often struggle with the inherent complexity of real-world systems, requiring rigid structures and extensive data. This research explores the potential of self-organizing networks to effectively model these systems by leveraging their ability to dynamically adapt and learn patterns without explicit supervision. We present a framework that utilizes a self-organizing network to represent the system's state and dynamics, enabling the model to capture intricate relationships and predict future states with improved accuracy. This approach offers a promising alternative to conventional machine learning techniques, particularly for complex systems where traditional methods fall short. The model's architecture is designed to be adaptable and capable of handling varying input data types, making it a versatile tool for diverse applications. title: Self-Adaptive Geometry Transformation Verification
abstract: This paper explores the application of quantum computing to the verification of geometric transformations, specifically focusing on a novel approach based on adaptive topology. The core mechanism involves quantum state manipulation and analysis to assess the fidelity and stability of the transformation. The resulting quantum verification process offers a potentially transformative approach to geometric analysis, particularly in areas involving complex geometries and high-dimensional transformations. This research establishes a new foundation for quantum-assisted geometric verification, highlighting the potential for significant advancements across diverse computational fields.

title: Meta-Learning with Bayesian Optimization for Neural Network Architecture Search
abstract: This paper presents a novel approach to neural network architecture search (NAS) leveraging meta-learning and Bayesian optimization. Traditional NAS methods often suffer from high computational costs associated with exhaustive or reinforcement learning-based exploration of the architecture search space. Our method, Bayesian Optimization with a Gaussian Process surrogate model, offers a significantly more efficient alternative. We learn from previous architecture search trials, using this knowledge to guide the selection of promising architectures in subsequent searches. This meta-learning framework allows us to rapidly converge on high-performing architectures, reducing the overall search time while maintaining competitive accuracy. The core of our approach lies in the use of a Gaussian Process to model the performance of different neural network architectures, and then employing an acquisition function to intelligently guide the exploration of the architecture space. This paper details the formulation of the problem, the implementation of the Bayesian optimization algorithm, and demonstrates its effectiveness through theoretical analysis and a discussion of the key components.

title: Probabilistic Logic Graph Evolution
abstract: This paper proposes a novel approach to knowledge representation and reasoning under uncertainty by leveraging evolutionary computation. The core idea is to simulate biological evolution to automatically generate and optimize probabilistic logic graphs (PLGs). These PLGs are designed to represent and reason with uncertain knowledge. We utilize genetic algorithms and simulated annealing algorithms to drive the evolution of PLGs, adapting their structure and parameters to changing environmental conditions and knowledge bases. The key innovation lies in combining evolutionary algorithms with PLGs, offering a dynamic and adaptive system compared to traditional static logic inference methods. The resulting system demonstrates the potential for self-organizing knowledge representation and reasoning, particularly in scenarios with incomplete or evolving information. We present a theoretical framework and explore the fundamental mechanisms driving this evolutionary process.

title: Asian Musk Shrew: A Novel Metaheuristic Algorithm Inspired by Foraging Behavior
abstract: This paper presents a new metaheuristic algorithm, termed "Asian Musk Shrew" (AMS), inspired by the foraging behavior of the Asian musk shrew (Suncus murinus). The algorithm leverages the shrew's efficient and adaptive foraging strategy—specifically, its tendency to explore promising areas while maintaining a balance between exploitation and exploration—to solve complex optimization problems. AMS incorporates key aspects of the shrew's behavior, including a novel movement strategy based on a combination of random walks and gradient descent, and a dynamic adjustment of the exploration probability. The algorithm utilizes a population-based approach, employing a swarm of potential solutions and iteratively refining them through interactions governed by a fitness function. We demonstrate the effectiveness of AMS through several benchmark problems, showcasing its ability to converge to optimal or near-optimal solutions with competitive performance compared to established metaheuristic methods such as Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO) and Genetic Algorithm (GA). The algorithm's parameters are designed to mimic the shrew's adaptability and response to environmental changes, leading to robust performance across diverse problem landscapes. The core of AMS lies in its adaptive exploration probability, which is dynamically adjusted based on the diversity within the population and the stagnation of the best solution. This ensures a balance between exploiting promising regions and continuing to explore the search space.

title: Meta-Learning for Machine Learning Model Optimization
abstract: This paper explores the application of meta-learning techniques to optimize the training process of machine learning models. Traditional model training relies heavily on manual hyperparameter tuning and careful selection of learning rates, often requiring significant time and expertise. This work proposes a meta-learning framework that learns how to learn, effectively automating the optimization process and aiming to improve the generalization performance of the resulting models. The core idea is to train a meta-learner on a distribution of learning tasks, allowing it to identify optimal training strategies for new, unseen tasks. This paper details the architecture of the meta-learning system, outlines the key components, and discusses the potential benefits and challenges associated with this approach. We demonstrate, conceptually, how this methodology could lead to more efficient and robust model training. ---

title: The Crimson-Headed Parrot Inspired Metaheuristic Optimization Algorithm (CHP-MHOA)
abstract: This paper introduces the Crimson-Headed Parrot Inspired Metaheuristic Optimization Algorithm (CHP-MHOA), a novel metaheuristic algorithm designed to address complex optimization problems. The algorithm's core inspiration stems from the foraging behavior and social dynamics observed in crimson-headed parrots, specifically their ability to efficiently locate food sources and adapt to changing environmental conditions. CHP-MHOA incorporates key elements of parrot behavior, including spatial distribution, flocking dynamics, and selective attention, into its search process. The algorithm utilizes a novel representation of the search space based on a multi-dimensional grid mimicking the parrot's foraging territory, and a dynamic agent system inspired by flocking behavior. A key innovation is the "Attention Mechanism," which selectively focuses the algorithm's efforts on promising regions of the search space, mirroring the parrot's focused attention on potential food sources. The algorithm's performance is evaluated theoretically, focusing on its adaptability and convergence properties. This paper details the algorithm's design, mathematical formulation, and theoretical analysis, laying the groundwork for future experimental validation.

title: Adaptive Software Architecture Based on Cognitive Computing
abstract: This paper proposes a novel adaptive software architecture based on cognitive computing principles. The core claim is to design an architecture capable of autonomously adjusting its structure and behavior based on changes within its operational environment, thereby enhancing its adaptability and robustness. This is achieved through the implementation of a cognitive computing mechanism that mimics human cognitive processes—specifically, perception, understanding, and decision-making—to dynamically respond to environmental shifts. The architecture utilizes key concepts like Bayesian Networks, Rule-Based Systems, and Reinforcement Learning to represent and reason about the system's state and guide architectural modifications. The proposed system aims to address limitations of traditional static architectures by introducing an intelligent, self-optimizing framework. The primary contributions of this work lie in the integration of cognitive techniques directly into the design and evolution of software architecture, providing a foundation for building more resilient and effective systems in dynamic and unpredictable environments. The paper details the architecture's components, the cognitive mechanisms employed, and a conceptual framework for its adaptation process. Further research will focus on developing practical implementation strategies and evaluating the architecture's performance in realistic scenarios.

title: Quantum State Collapse as a Computational Algorithm
abstract: Quantum state collapse is a fundamental aspect of quantum mechanics, yet its implications for computation remain largely unexplored. This paper proposes a novel computational algorithm based on the inherent probabilistic nature of quantum collapse to efficiently solve problems intractable with classical methods. We demonstrate this algorithm's potential for rapid evaluation of complex functions through a carefully designed 'quantum state collapse' process. The core mechanism centers around leveraging the uncertainty principle to dynamically adjust the state of a quantum system, effectively "collapsing" a state to reveal a solution. This represents a significant departure from traditional computational approaches, offering a potentially transformative paradigm for tackling computationally challenging problems in diverse fields.

title: Relational Causal Inference via Deep Generative Models
abstract: This paper introduces a novel approach to relational causal inference leveraging the capabilities of deep generative models. Traditional methods heavily rely on explicitly defined causal graphs, a process often hampered by complexity and reliance on assumptions. We propose a framework that directly learns relational causal structures from observational data using deep generative models. This eliminates the need for a pre-defined graph, offering a more flexible and potentially more accurate inference process. The core mechanism involves training a generative model to capture the underlying relationships between variables, enabling us to infer causal connections even when the true causal graph is unknown. We demonstrate the potential of this approach through a theoretical discussion and a detailed explanation of the methodology. The key contribution lies in the combination of generative modeling's representational power with relational causal inference, providing a robust solution for causal discovery and inference in complex scenarios. The ultimate goal is to provide a more reliable and adaptable method for understanding causal relationships in various domains. ---

The key contribution lies in the combination of generative modeling's representational power with relational causal inference, providing a robust solution for causal discovery and inference in complex scenarios. title: Distributed Bayesian Inference with Federated Learning and Differential Privacy
abstract: This paper presents a novel approach to distributed Bayesian inference that leverages the strengths of federated learning and differential privacy. The core idea is to execute Bayesian inference locally on a network of devices, aggregating updates while simultaneously protecting individual privacy. We introduce a framework where each device independently performs Bayesian inference on its local data and then adds noise to the updates based on differential privacy guarantees. This ensures that no single device's contribution can be identified, thus preserving privacy. The resulting system achieves accurate Bayesian inference across a decentralized network, offering a practical solution for privacy-sensitive data analysis. This work provides a new method for distributed learning which combines Bayesian inference, federated learning and differential privacy.

title: Adaptive Evolutionary Metaheuristic with Neural Feedback
abstract: This paper presents a novel approach to metaheuristic optimization by integrating neural networks for adaptive feedback. The core idea is to utilize a neural network to analyze the state of a metaheuristic algorithm in real-time and provide dynamic adjustments to its parameters. This contrasts with traditional metaheuristic methods that rely on fixed or pre-defined parameter settings. The proposed method, termed Adaptive Evolutionary Metaheuristic with Neural Feedback (AEMNF), employs a neural network to process the algorithm's internal state, including parameters like step size and learning rate, alongside gradient information from the objective function. The network's output then informs adjustments to these parameters, enabling the algorithm to self-adapt its search strategy and potentially achieve superior optimization performance. Experimental results, though not presented here due to the focus on the methodology, demonstrate the potential of this approach. The key innovation lies in shifting the role of neural networks from solely evaluating objective function values to actively controlling the adaptive behavior of the metaheuristic itself.

title: The Amazonian Asp Snake Metaheuristic Algorithm (AASMA)
abstract: This paper introduces the Amazonian Asp Snake Metaheuristic Algorithm (AASMA), a novel metaheuristic optimization algorithm inspired by the foraging behavior and movement patterns of *Corallus caninus* (Amazonian Asp Snake). The algorithm leverages the snake's unique ability to dynamically adjust its search space, exploit promising regions, and navigate complex landscapes to achieve efficient global optimization. AASMA incorporates key features such as adaptive movement strategies, a novel 'shedding' mechanism mimicking the snake's periodic renewal of scales, and a dynamic neighborhood structure reflecting the snake's flexible hunting behavior. Unlike traditional metaheuristics, AASMA prioritizes adaptability and exploration, leading to potentially faster convergence and improved solution quality. This paper outlines the algorithm's theoretical foundation, its core components, and its potential applications in various optimization problems. The algorithm's performance is discussed in terms of its parameters and their impact on the optimization process.

title: Title: Algorithmic Quantum Simulation of Complex Dynamical Systems
abstract: Quantum simulation holds immense promise for understanding and manipulating complex dynamical systems – phenomena ranging from fluid dynamics and climate modeling to protein folding and the behavior of complex chemical reactions. However, current simulation techniques face significant limitations, particularly when dealing with high-dimensional systems. This paper introduces an algorithmic quantum simulation framework, centered on a novel 'Quantum Monte Carlo' algorithm leveraging quantum entanglement to accelerate the solution of these systems, offering a fundamentally new approach to complex dynamics analysis. The core claim is to create a class of quantum algorithms designed to efficiently simulate and analyze complex dynamical systems, with a particular focus on uncovering critical patterns and dynamics that are difficult to discern with classical methods. This work explores the potential of entanglement as a key mechanism for accelerating the simulation process and provides a foundational outline for a new generation of quantum algorithms tailored for these challenging problems.

title: Title: Geometric Quantum State Representation & Manipulation
abstract: Quantum state representation and manipulation represent a fundamental challenge in quantum information science. Current methods often struggle with precision and scalability, hindering the development of complex quantum algorithms. This paper proposes a novel geometric representation for quantum states, leveraging entanglement and geometric operations to achieve unprecedented control and manipulation capabilities. The core mechanism centers around defining a 'Quantum State Vector' – a vector representing the state's geometry – allowing for precise transformation and manipulation through a combination of quantum entanglement and geometric transformations. We demonstrate the efficacy of this approach through rigorous mathematical analysis and illustrative examples, highlighting its potential to surpass current limitations in quantum state manipulation.

title: Quantum Information in Chemical Reaction Rate Prediction
abstract: Quantum information has emerged as a transformative tool across diverse fields, and its potential within chemical reaction rate prediction is increasingly attracting attention. This paper explores the integration of quantum information and geometric modeling to enhance the prediction of reaction rates, utilizing geometric information for optimization. We present a novel framework that leverages quantum algorithms to represent chemical reaction dynamics as geometric functions, enabling the optimization of reaction conditions based on these geometric representations. The core mechanism focuses on translating complex reaction kinetics into a simplified geometric model, allowing for efficient optimization through geometric analysis. The study demonstrates the effectiveness of this approach in predicting reaction rates, offering a promising pathway towards improved reaction control and understanding.

title: Self-Adaptive Quantum State Computation
abstract: This paper introduces a novel self-adaptive quantum state computation paradigm designed to enhance quantum multi-body calculations. Traditional approaches often focus on static state representations, limiting the system's complexity and computational efficiency. Our work proposes a dynamic adjustment mechanism within the quantum state, enabling the simulation and optimization of intricate quantum systems. We demonstrate the efficacy of this approach through a series of simulations, highlighting its potential to significantly improve computational speed and accuracy compared to existing methods. The core mechanism centers on dynamically adjusting the quantum state to achieve complex system behavior and, ultimately, reduce computational costs. This research offers a fundamentally new perspective on quantum multi-body calculations, paving the way for more efficient and powerful simulations.

title: ## The Mimicry-Guided Adaptive Search (MGAS) Algorithm: An Inspiration from Short-tailed Atheris
abstract: This paper introduces the Mimicry-Guided Adaptive Search (MGAS) algorithm, a novel metaheuristic optimization technique inspired by the foraging behavior and camouflage strategies of the short-tailed Atheris (short-tailed shrew). The algorithm leverages the principle of mimicry – the short-tailed Atheris's ability to imitate successful foraging patterns of other individuals – combined with adaptive parameter adjustment to navigate complex search spaces. MGAS employs a population-based approach, where each individual represents a potential solution. The algorithm's core mechanism involves mimicking successful solutions within the population, dynamically adjusting the mimicry rate and exploration/exploitation balance based on the diversity and convergence characteristics of the population. The algorithm's performance is evaluated through theoretical analysis, demonstrating its potential for efficient exploration and exploitation in various optimization problems. Key features include a dynamic mimicry ratio, a population diversity preservation mechanism, and an adaptive step size control.

title: AI-Driven Marketing Analytics for Predicting Customer Preferences for Eco-Friendly Excavators in the Indian Construction Equipment Market
abstract: Abstract The integration of Artificial Intelligence (AI) into marketing is transforming the way organisations understand customer preferences, predict buying behaviour and design personalised marketing strategies. In the construction equipment industry, increasing environmental concerns, emission requirements and demand for fuel-efficient technologies have created a need for more effective approaches to promote eco-friendly excavators. This study proposes an empirical investigation of the role of AI-driven marketing analytics in predicting customer preferences for eco-friendly excavators in the Indian construction equipment market. Drawing upon the Theory of Planned Behavior (TPB) and the Antecedents-Decisions-Outcomes (ADO) framework, the study examines the influence of AI-enabled personalisation, predictive analytics, environmental awareness and perceived usefulness of AI-based recommendations on customer preference for eco-friendly excavators. The study focuses on construction contractors, equipment purchasers and other industrial decision-makers involved in excavator procurement. A structured questionnaire using a five-point Likert scale is proposed for primary data collection. Descriptive statistics, reliability analysis, correlation and regression analysis can be employed to examine the proposed relationships. The study contributes to sustainable marketing literature by connecting AI-driven marketing analytics with industrial customer preferences in the heavy construction equipment sector. The empirical statistics reported in this manuscript are based on a simulated dataset of 212 respondents and are intended for demonstration only.

title: Beyond Suspicion Scores: Competing-Explanation Inference for Fraud-Shaped Legitimate Activity
abstract: Fraud detection systems commonly score suspiciousness and act when a score crosses a threshold. This is unreliable when legitimate activity exhibits fraud-like structure: in our diagnostic corpus, structurally suspicious legitimate cases carry more fraud-shaped relational structure than genuine fraud does, and every purely structural statistic we evaluated ranked them above fraud. We present AFIE, a knowledge-based evidentiary architecture that treats fraud recognition as adjudication between competing explanations rather than accumulation of suspicion. A case likelihood is composed on a bounded log-odds scale as L0 + F + M - B - C, combining affirmative fraud-semantic evidence (F) grouped into coherent mechanisms, gated mature recognition (M), affirmative exculpatory evidence (B), and contradiction evidence (C). The architecture is recomputed from the current evidence state at each observation prefix, has no absorbing state, and treats the absence of exculpatory evidence as contributing exactly zero. Its principal contribution is an evidentiary admissibility rule for mature recognition: a completed exemplar is admitted only when it is persistent, positively informative relative to locally estimated ordinary opportunity, a member of the coherent mechanism selected by the affirmative channel, situated in a mechanism whose net evidence supports fraud, and not covered by applicable exculpatory evidence. On a 160-case authored all-comers corpus with semantically adequate documentary evidence, the architecture attains an area under the ROC curve of 0.904 at the final prefix, with final-prefix AUC 0.904 (95% bootstrap CI [0.847, 0.952]), complete mature-fraud detection, zero observed escalation across both legitimate families, 4.3% dangerous under-detection, and 0/1,600 prefix-isolation leakage violations. We report negative findings in full, including the failure of graph-coherence formulations and of an emerging-before-mature hypothesis. The evaluation is a local mechanism proof on an authored corpus and is not independent validation.

title: APPLICATION OF ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE IN INTENSIVE CARE: CLINICAL POTENTIAL AND CHALLENGES
abstract: Background: Contemporary intensive care units (ICUs) generate vast amounts of real-time data, leading to staff cognitive overload and the phenomenon of alarm fatigue. Traditional prognostic scoring systems (APACHE II, SOFA) are inherently static and fail to account for dynamic clinical trends. Artificial intelligence (AI) algorithms, including machine learning (ML) and deep learning (DL), offer novel capabilities for continuous monitoring and early prediction of life-threatening conditions. Objective: To analyze the clinical potential and implementation challenges associated with the deployment of AI algorithms in intensive care settings. Methods: A comprehensive literature review was conducted across the PubMed, Embase, and IEEE Xplore databases for the years 2018–2026, focusing on studies utilizing multicenter databases (such as MIMIC-IV and eICU). Results: AI algorithms demonstrate high discriminative performance (AUROC 0.79–0.96) in the early detection of sepsis, prediction of hemodynamic instability with a 5-to-15-minute lead time, and dynamic mortality risk estimation. In the context of mechanical ventilation, deep learning models (specifically convolutional neural networks, CNNs) enable automated detection of patient-ventilator asynchrony with an accuracy exceeding 90%, as well as precise forecasting of extubation success. Conclusions: Artificial intelligence holds immense potential for optimizing ICU patient care. However, primary implementation barriers persist, including the lack of model interpretability (the "black box" problem), domain shift, and ethico-psychological dilemmas, such as clinician moral distress and the risk of care dehumanization. AI systems should function strictly as clinical decision support tools under physician supervision.

title: A Computational Framework for Cross-Temporal Sentiment and Topic Analysis of Reddit Data
abstract: This paper develops and validates a modular computational framework for longitudinal sentiment and thematic analysis of unstructured social media data. While computational social science increasingly relies on automated tools, a gap remains in validated pipelines that rigorously integrate temporal dynamics with reliable sentiment metrics for noisy text. The proposed technical contribution is a three-stage pipeline comprising: (1) a comparative validation protocol establishing the superiority of lexicon-based rules (VADER) over un-tuned transformers (BERT) for specific informal domains; (2) a hybrid hierarchical topic modeling approach; and (3) a robust regression architecture cross-validated with LightGBM machine learning models. The framework's engineering utility is demonstrated through a 15-year dataset (N = 2267) of cross-cultural Reddit discourse. Results confirm the pipeline's ability to reliably detect event-driven signal shifts and isolate feature importance. This study offers engineers and data scientists a validated, replicable solution for high-noise public opinion mining and crisis monitoring applications.

title: A Study on LLM-based Game NPC State Control using FSM
abstract: 최근 LLM(Large Language Model)을 활용한 게임 NPC는 플레이어의 자연어 입력에 따라 유연하고 자연스러운 대화를 제공할 수 있다. 그러나 LLM 기반 NPC의 자유로운 응답은 현재 게임 상태나 기획 의도와 맞지 않는 행동으로 이어질 수 있으며, 거래, 퀘스트, 보상, 전투와 같은 시스템과 연결될 경우 비허용 상태 전이가 발생할 수 있다. 본 논문에서는 LLM 기반 NPC의 대화 능력을 유지하면서도, 게임 규칙을 벗어난 행동이 실제 시스템에 반영되지 않도록 FSM 기반 가드레일 구조를 제안한다. 제안 구조는 LLM이 플레이어 입력을 JSON 형식의 intent와 ruleTags로 변환하고, FSM이 현재 게임 상태와 규칙을 검증한 뒤 상태 전이 허용 여부를 결정하는 방식이다. Unity 기반 NPC 상호작용 환경에서 LLM-only 방식과 LLM+FSM 방식을 비교한 결과, 비허용 입력에 대한 금지 상태 전이의 발생을 감소시켰으며, 정상 입력의 성공률을 향상시켰다.

title: Delegation Without Trust: An Empirical Gap Analysis of Identity, Authorization, and Runtime Governance in Multi-Agent LLM Systems
abstract: Autonomous LLM agents increasingly act on a user's behalf: they hold credentials, call tools and services, and spawn sub-agents that act further on their behalf. This turns a long-standing distributed-systems question -- who is authorized to do what, on whose authority -- into an urgent and largely unsolved problem, because the component driving each agent is a language model an adversary can hijack. We argue that agent security must be evaluated under an untrusted-model assumption: a correct system is one in which a fully prompt-injected agent still cannot exceed the authority explicitly delegated to it. Against this standard we make three contributions. title: Learning the Geometry of Admissible Hypotheses through Inductive Bias in Training Distributions
abstract: Scientific discovery often requires reasoning over competing hypotheses that are consistent with experimental observations. For mixed-variable and combinatorial hypothesis spaces, however, constructing probabilistic representations remains challenging because both the active model components and their associated parameters are unknown. In this work, we present a framework for learning continuous latent representations of admissible partial differential equations (PDEs) by embedding a scientific inductive bias directly into the training distribution. Progressively richer structural principles (e.g., sparsity, logical dependencies, common PDE families, and physical admissibility) are used to generate a structured distribution of hypotheses from which a gated variational autoencoder learns a continuous latent manifold. Experimental results show that the resulting 11-dimensional representation accurately reconstructs a broad collection of representative PDEs, while exhibiting smooth geometric transitions both within and across equation families. Through an ablation study we further demonstrate that introducing scientific principles reduces both structural misclassifications of equation forms and parameter estimation errors when reconstructing a representative benchmark set of admissible partial differential equations. These results show that embedding a scientific inductive bias in the training distribution enables the learning of compact and geometrically meaningful hypothesis manifolds, providing a principled foundation for future inference over competing governing equations.

title: Constrained minimax approximation for quantum signal processing
abstract: Quantum signal processing (QSP) provides a simple and efficient framework for implementing polynomial transformations using quantum circuits. Its classical design stage leads to a constrained minimax approximation problem: find a polynomial of prescribed parity that approximates a target function uniformly on a fitting set while remaining bounded in magnitude by one on the domain $[0,1]$, which can be viewed as a semi-infinite constraint. Discretization converts the problem into a linear program, but feasibility at a set of finitely many sampled points does not ensure feasibility on the whole domain, especially when an optimal approximant reaches the boundary of the feasible set. We investigate two approaches to address this difficulty. A Remez exchange method combined with active-set constraint enforcement is efficient on many tested instances, but its stability depends on the target and problem geometry. We then introduce nonlinear Fourier retraction, which uses QSP completion and phase synthesis to turn a nearly feasible polynomial into phase factors for a feasible QSP polynomial without increasing the degree. Across representative problems, retraction largely preserves approximation accuracy and remains effective on instances where the Remez heuristic is unstable. The resulting workflow connects classical minimax approximation and semi-infinite optimization with nonlinear Fourier analysis, and is implemented in the qsppack software package.

title: TrainSDC: Characterizing and Mitigating Silent Data Corruption in Large Language Model Training
abstract: LLM training is increasingly vulnerable to silent data corruption (SDC), yet existing protection methods largely treat Transformer computations uniformly because their vulnerability remains poorly understood. We present the first systematic characterization of SDC vulnerability across major computation interfaces in both the forward and backward passes of Transformer training. Our analysis reveals two distinct error propagation mechanisms: forward-pass vulnerability is highly location dependent, with faults on the Q/K path producing persistent training deviations, whereas backward-pass vulnerability is largely governed by gradient exponent distributions rather than computation locations. Motivated by these observations, we propose TrainSDC, a characterization-guided protection framework consisting of Q/K-path recomputation, residual-gain monitoring, and exponent-aware gradient scaling. Experiments on Llama 3.2-1B and Qwen3-0.6B show that TrainSDC maintains training behavior close to fault-free execution under both sparse and dense fault injection while introducing only 1.65%-6.76% runtime overhead.

title: Designing an Auditable LLM-Supported Workflow for Qualitative Thematic Analysis
abstract: Large Language Models (LLMs) offer new possibilities for scaling qualitative analysis, but existing applications often provide limited methodological transparency regarding how qualitative methods are translated into computational procedures. This paper presents an auditable and privacy-preserving computational operationalization of inductive and latent Thematic Analysis (TA). This paper first derives five design principles from the methodological requirements of TA and the conditions introduced by LLM-based inference: preserving interpretative context, maintaining traceable relationships between empirical material and analytical outputs, representing analytical constructs and reasoning explicitly, constraining LLM inference to interpretative tasks, and enabling privacy-preserving local deployment. Second, it presents a proof-of-concept for a two-phase workflow that operationalizes these principles by combining interpretative LLM inference with deterministic procedural control to generate codes, analytical justifications, themes, and theme descriptions while preserving explicit links to the source material. Third, it proposes an evaluation framework combining structural comparison with human-led TA and independent expert assessment of analytical quality. The evaluation is conducted on semi-structured Danish interview transcripts. and the results shows that the workflow produces code-level outputs with coverage broadly comparable to human annotations and highly rated analytical justifications, while generating a more compressed thematic structure characterized by fewer and broader themes. The findings demonstrate the feasibility of auditable LLM-supported TA through a modular workflow designed to scale to larger datasets, accommodate different LLMs, and support transfer across research domains, with domain adaptation primarily requiring adjustments to the prompting strategy.

title: Beyond Ranking Accuracy: Evaluating LLM-Cited Feature Rationales for Next Basket Repurchase Recommendation
abstract: Next-basket repurchase recommendation is commonly formulated as a ranking task: given a customer's purchase history, the system ranks previously purchased items that may be needed again. In production settings, however, ranking accuracy is only one component of recommendation quality. Customers may also benefit from concise evidence about why an item is recommended now. Large language models (LLMs) offer a potential way to surface such evidence through feature-based, human-readable rationales grounded in interpretable behavioral signals. We construct repurchase features spanning cadence, frequency, recency, user behavior, and item popularity, and evaluate LLMs on two public grocery datasets and one proprietary retail dataset. We investigate (1) whether off-the-shelf LLMs can use these features as next-basket scorers relative to heuristic and supervised rankers, and (2) whether LLM-cited features carry outcome-grounded ranking signal. For the latter, we compare LLM-cited features with model-specific attribution methods under a cross-model feature-masking protocol that measures ranking degradation after masking selected features. Our results show that LLM scores are not competitive with supervised rankers, suggesting that off-the-shelf LLMs should not be used as standalone repurchase recommenders. However, changes in prompt and evidence representation can improve outcome-grounded feature-masking results in some settings even when ranking performance does not improve; the effect is dataset-dependent and does not consistently match attribution baselines. These findings suggest a practical role for LLMs as validated explanation components rather than primary rankers, with rationale quality evaluated separately from ranking accuracy.

title: การออกแบบและพฒนาเทคโนโลยแชทบอทเพอสนบสนนการเรยนการสอน
abstract: This research aimed to design and develop a chatbot to support teaching and learning in a prototype course and to assess students' satisfaction with its use. The chatbot was developed using the Dialogflow platform and integrated into the LINE application. This chatbot was designed to respond to inquiries and provide information pertaining to the academic courses 000204 Digital Game and 503220 Computer Engineering Drawing. It was designed to respond to students' inquiries and provide information 24 hours a day, enhancing the learning experience by allowing quick and convenient access to course-related information. The satisfaction evaluation focused on three key aspects: content accuracy, usability, and practical application. The results showed that students were highly satisfied with the chatbot, particularly regarding the accuracy and timeliness of the information provided, which received the highest average satisfaction score of 4.23. In terms of usability, students appreciated the chatbot's fast response time, with an average satisfaction score of 4.23. Regarding its practical application in helping students understand the course material, the average satisfaction score was 4.17. In conclusion, the chatbot effectively met students' needs by delivering fast, accurate, and accessible information. Students expressed high satisfaction, indicating that the chatbot is a valuable tool for supporting teaching and learning.

title: Machine Learning-based Virtual Densification of Sparse Environmental Variables (Solar Radiation and PM10) from Co-located Basic Weather Observations across South Korea
abstract: Among the weather networks in South Korea, although basic variables are recorded at 600 to 744 stations nationwide, only approximately 67 and 31 are equipped with sensors for detecting solar radiation (GSR) and particulate matter (PM10), respectively. Exploiting this asymmetry, we propose a machine-learning-based virtual densification to facilitate estimations of sparse variables from co-located basic-weather variables, evaluated based on leave-station-out (LSO) cross-validation, excluding entire stations to emulate sensor-free locations. Solar radiation was found to be effectively densified (LSO R2 = 0.76 ± 0.03), far exceeding the Hargreaves-Samani baseline (R2 = 0.54) and was stable without coordinates, indicating a physical relationship. Comparatively, PM10 reaches only R2 = 0.28 from weather alone, a control for emission-driven variables. Although machine learning (RandomForest, XGBoost) achieves significantly higher predictive accuracy than the empirical and linear baselines (p < 0.001), the two models are mutually indistinguishable. Given that solar radiation is a required wet-bulb globe temperature input, the virtual solar field can directly support heat-disaster risk assessment in locations in which sensors are absent.

title: Non-Linear Geometric Topology Quantum Algorithms
abstract: This paper explores the application of non-linear geometric topology in quantum algorithms to enhance computational efficiency and uncover novel geometric features. The core focus is on leveraging quantum entanglement and self-adaptive mechanisms to devise quantum algorithms that surpass classical limitations. We investigate how these techniques can facilitate the manipulation of complex geometric structures, ultimately leading to significant improvements in data analysis and computational speed. The study aims to identify specific geometric patterns and their associated quantum properties, offering a pathway toward advancements in data processing and potentially revolutionizing computational paradigms.

title: Adaptive Quantum Topology Simulation
abstract: This paper introduces an adaptive quantum topology simulation framework designed to automate the adjustment of topological structures and facilitate accurate and efficient topology simulations. Traditional topological simulation methods rely on manual design of the topology, which is limited in its adaptability to evolving data. Our approach leverages a dynamic quantum topology structure, employing quantum topology simulation algorithms to dynamically adjust the topology during the simulation process. This innovation addresses a key limitation of existing methods, offering a more robust and versatile approach to topology exploration. The core mechanism focuses on establishing a self-regulating quantum topology, allowing for automated adaptation to complex and dynamic topological landscapes. We demonstrate the framework's efficacy through illustrative examples, showcasing its ability to successfully simulate topological phases and navigate challenging geometries. This work represents a significant advancement in the field, providing a new methodology for topological exploration and simulation.

title: Dynamic Adaptive Probability Model
abstract: This paper introduces a novel dynamic adaptive probability model, designed to address the limitations of traditional probability models in dynamic environments. The model employs a dynamic probability update mechanism, driven by learning data and environmental information, to dynamically adjust model parameters and automatically learn new model structures. This allows for more accurate predictions and decisions in real-time. The core mechanism centers around a learning-based parameter adjustment process, combined with reinforcement learning techniques for structural adaptation. The benefits of this approach include enhanced adaptability, improved predictive accuracy, and automated model refinement. This work presents a framework for creating a model capable of continuous learning and optimization across diverse scenarios.

title: Meta-Learning for Continual Learning: A Rapid Adaptation Framework
abstract: This paper proposes a novel continual learning framework based on meta-learning, designed to facilitate rapid adaptation of models across diverse tasks. Traditional continual learning methods often struggle with the inherent variability between tasks, frequently relying on techniques like transfer learning that can be sensitive to task differences. Our approach leverages the core principle of meta-learning – learning *how* to learn – to enable the model to efficiently acquire knowledge and generalize across a sequence of tasks. The framework utilizes meta-learning algorithms to optimize the learning process itself, leading to improved performance and reduced catastrophic forgetting. We demonstrate the effectiveness of this approach through a theoretical analysis and outline the key components, focusing on the adaptive learning rate and task-specific regularization strategies within the meta-learning loop. The resulting system offers a more robust and efficient solution for continual learning compared to conventional methods.

title: 基于量子自适应的机器学习的生成模型优化
abstract: This paper introduces a novel generative model optimization strategy leveraging the principles of quantum self-adaptation. Traditional optimization methods often require manual tuning of model parameters, which can be time-consuming and suboptimal. We propose a quantum self-adaptation approach that dynamically adjusts the parameters of a generative model through quantum computations, leading to improved generation quality and efficiency. The core mechanism centers around quantum state manipulation to automatically optimize the model's output distribution. This approach offers a significant advantage over existing methods by automating the parameter adjustment process and potentially unlocking enhanced generative capabilities. We present a theoretical framework and preliminary experimental results demonstrating the effectiveness of this quantum-enhanced optimization strategy.

title: 基于生物神经网络的计算生物学模型优化
abstract: This paper proposes a novel approach to optimizing computational biology models by leveraging the principles of biological neural networks. Traditional methods for model optimization often rely on heuristic search algorithms and manual parameter tuning, which can be computationally expensive and yield suboptimal results. Our approach transforms computational biology models into a network of interconnected weights, analogous to the connections in a biological neural network. We then utilize adaptive learning algorithms inspired by biological neural networks to iteratively refine these weights, aiming to improve model accuracy and efficiency. The core of this method lies in the mapping of the model's parameters and structure to a neural network architecture, allowing for the exploitation of the inherent learning capabilities of biological systems. We demonstrate the potential of this approach through a conceptual framework, outlining the key steps involved and highlighting the advantages over conventional optimization techniques. This work provides a foundation for future research exploring the integration of biological neural network optimization strategies within the field of computational biology.

title: Quantum Computation Optimization Based on Quantum Decoherence
abstract: This paper explores the potential of leveraging quantum decoherence in distributed computing environments for optimizing complex problems. The core concept involves utilizing controlled entanglement to facilitate rapid approximation of global optimal solutions. The approach decomposes the optimization problem into sub-problems, each assigned to a quantum node. Quantum entanglement enables synchronized information exchange and collaborative computation among these nodes. Furthermore, decoherence suppression techniques are incorporated to enhance the accuracy of the computations. We propose a framework where the inherent properties of quantum decoherence are strategically employed to overcome limitations in traditional optimization algorithms, particularly in scenarios demanding high computational throughput and scalability. The theoretical framework presented here lays the groundwork for future research and development in this nascent field. The primary focus remains on the conceptual design and outlining of the core mechanisms, without the inclusion of experimental validation.

title: Title: Adaptive Topology for Quantum Simulation of Condensed Matter
abstract: Quantum simulation of condensed matter systems offers unprecedented insights into their behavior, but current methods often struggle to accurately represent the complex dynamics and intricate topologies. title: Automated Theorem Proving via Large Language Model Orchestration
abstract: This paper investigates the potential of Large Language Models (LLMs) to contribute to automated theorem proving. The core idea is to orchestrate an LLM through a series of carefully designed steps within the theorem proving process. This involves leveraging the LLM's ability to understand and generate natural language, combined with a structured prompt engineering approach, to handle tasks such as hypothesis formulation, lemma retrieval, and inference verification. We explore a system architecture where the LLM acts as a central component, executing specific tasks based on prompts and iteratively refining its approach. The novelty lies in applying LLMs to formal proof systems rather than solely relying on traditional automated reasoning techniques. We demonstrate the feasibility of this approach through conceptual design and outline a strategy for effective prompt engineering, highlighting the challenges and potential avenues for future research. The goal is to create a system that can assist mathematicians and logicians in their work, and potentially accelerate the discovery of new mathematical knowledge.

title: Title: Hyper-Resonant Quantum Simulation (HRQS)
abstract: This paper presents the Hyper-Resonant Quantum Simulation (HRQS) method, a novel approach to quantum system simulation that significantly reduces computational cost through a refined resonant frequency mapping algorithm. Traditional quantum simulation methods are often plagued by exponential scaling with system size, making them impractical for many real-world problems. HRQS addresses this limitation by dynamically identifying and focusing computational effort on the most relevant resonant frequencies, drastically decreasing the computational demands. We detail the algorithm's architecture, demonstrate its effectiveness through simulations of a simple quantum system, and discuss future research directions. The core claim is that HRQS provides a substantial improvement in computational efficiency compared to existing quantum simulation techniques, offering a pathway toward more accessible and efficient quantum modeling.

title: Quantum Simulation-Driven Materials Discovery
abstract: This paper explores the transformative potential of quantum simulation for accelerating materials discovery. Classical computational methods often struggle with the complexities of simulating quantum mechanical systems, particularly for materials exhibiting strong electron correlations. Quantum simulation offers a fundamentally different approach, leveraging the principles of quantum mechanics to directly model these systems on a quantum computer. This work outlines the key concepts, methodologies, and potential impact of this emerging field. We present a framework for utilizing quantum computers to simulate material properties, including electronic structure, magnetic behavior, and transport characteristics. Specifically, we discuss the use of Variational Quantum Eigensolver (VQE) and Trotterization methods for solving the Schrödinger equation. The core claim is that quantum simulation will revolutionize materials discovery by enabling precise predictions of material properties and accelerating the identification of novel materials with desired characteristics. Furthermore, we address the current limitations and future directions of this technology, emphasizing the need for robust quantum hardware and sophisticated algorithms. ---

The core mechanism revolves around a dynamically evolving network of constraint nodes, ensuring optimal data representation. This work addresses a critical challenge in sensor data fusion by providing a robust and adaptable framework for data integration.

title: ## The Bio-Inspired Harmony Search Algorithm for Multi-Objective Optimization
abstract: This paper introduces the Harmony Search Algorithm (HSA), a novel metaheuristic optimization algorithm inspired by the foraging behavior of tiger prawn ( *Penaeus monodon* ). The algorithm mimics the prawns' harmonious search for food sources, utilizing a harmony pool, a harmony memory, and a dynamic harmony adjustment mechanism. The core principle lies in the prawns' ability to identify and select the best food sources within their environment through a process of iterative refinement and harmonic convergence. The HSA aims to address the challenges of traditional metaheuristic algorithms by incorporating a more robust exploration-exploitation balance and a mechanism for adapting to complex, multi-dimensional search spaces. This paper details the algorithm's design, operational principles, and theoretical foundations, highlighting its potential applicability across various optimization problems. The algorithm's performance is evaluated through a conceptual analysis, focusing on its adaptability and convergence characteristics, without requiring empirical experimentation.

title: Quantum Resource Allocation Based on Quantum Demagnetization
abstract: This paper investigates a novel approach to optimizing quantum computing resource allocation, leveraging the inherent characteristics of quantum demagnetization (decoherence). Traditional quantum resource allocation methods often rely on heuristic rules or empirical observations, lacking a fundamental understanding of the resource consumption mechanisms within a quantum system. This work posits that decoherence, a primary source of error and resource depletion in quantum computation, can be explicitly modeled and utilized as a constraint within an optimization framework. We present a methodology for allocating quantum resources—specifically, qubit assignments and gate scheduling—based on a dynamic assessment of decoherence rates. The core concept involves formulating a mathematical model where decoherence is treated as a cost function, and employing optimization algorithms to minimize this cost while satisfying computational requirements. The proposed method offers a potentially more efficient and targeted approach to resource allocation, leading to improvements in quantum computation efficiency and potentially mitigating the detrimental effects of decoherence. The results demonstrate the feasibility and effectiveness of this approach in theoretical scenarios.
